hero.title: Master's in Computer Engineering in Italy for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: Pursue an English-taught Laurea Magistrale in Computer Engineering in Italy at world-renowned polytechnics, mastering embedded systems, industrial robotics, affordable tuition, and a 12-month post-study job search permit.

highlights.eligibility: Recognised academic qualification + English / Italian proficiency

overview: Italy's advanced industrial economy relies extensively on sophisticated embedded computing systems, precision microcontrollers, and automated robotics across its Northern manufacturing belt. Pursuing a master's degree in Computer Engineering (*Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Informatica*) in Italy gives Indian students world-class engineering training in designing intelligent hardware-software systems.

Leading Italian polytechnics—including Politecnico di Milano, Politecnico di Torino, and the University of Bologna—offer 2-year English-taught Master of Science degrees (120 ECTS). The curriculum covers Advanced Microprocessor Architectures, Embedded Systems & Real-Time OS, Hardware-Software Co-Design, Cyber-Physical Systems, and Industrial Robotics, with very accessible public tuition (€1,000 to €4,000/year) and widespread eligibility for need-based regional DSU scholarships.

Graduates obtain credentials recognized throughout the European Higher Education Area (EHEA). Non-EU Master's and doctoral graduates are eligible to apply for a 12-month post-study residence permit (*Permesso di Soggiorno per Ricerca Lavoro o Imprenditorialità*, Art. 39-bis.1 TUI) to seek skilled engineering employment across Italy's Northern industrial technology corridor and European hardware enterprises.

sections.title: Who can Study Computer Engineering in Italy?

items: Generally, Indian students applying for a Master's in Computer Engineering in Italy should fulfill the following requirements:
Bachelor's degree: A recognized degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, Electronics or related discipline acceptable to the university.
Relevant academic subjects: Students may need to have completed previous coursework in programming, mathematics, algorithms, computer architecture, electronics or related subjects.
Academic performance: Meet the minimum grade, CGPA or academic assessment standards of the university.
English proficiency Fulfill the English language requirement for English-language programs. Various accepted tests and possible exemptions.
Knowledge of Italian: Required if the course of study is taught in Italian.
Academic Compatibility: The university will verify transcripts and completed credits to determine if your bachelor's degree is compatible with the program.
Additional selection requirements: An interview, motivation letter, CV or other assessment may be required.
Students in other undergraduate majors may be considered if they are adequately prepared in relevant areas, though admission is not guaranteed.

Admission Procedure for Computer Engineering in Italy
How to Earn a Master's Degree In Computer Engineering in Italy .
Choose your specialty: Decide whether you want to focus on software, AI, embedded systems, cybersecurity, networks or another area of computing.
Shortlist universities: Compare course content, language of instruction, fees and scholarship options.
Academic eligibility: Check the undergraduate subjects, credits and minimum grades needed.
Prepare your documents: Collect your degree certificate, transcripts, CV, language scores and supporting documents.
Apply for programs: Submit your application via the official university admissions portal within the application window.
Complete selection requirements: Attend any required interviews and provide any additional academic information.
Accept your offer: Follow the instructions from the university to confirm your admission and make any necessary payments.
Finish pre-enrolment and visa procedures: Check the official Universitaly portal and follow the instructions for international students that are currently available.
Final registration: Furnish any remaining documents and complete the registration process according to university instructions.
Begin early, as application deadlines differ across universities, programs and intakes.

sections.title: Computer Engineering Salary and Job Opportunities in Italy

items: Graduates of a Master's in Computer Engineering in Italy can find employment in software development, AI, telecommunications, cybersecurity, embedded systems and technology research.
Possible career paths include:
Computer Engineer: Designs, develops, and maintains computer based systems.
Software Engineer - Designs, builds and tests software applications and platforms.
Machine Learning and AI Engineer: Creates intelligent systems and machine-learning applications.
Embedded Systems Engineer: Design of software that integrates with hardware systems.
Cybersecurity Engineer: Helps protect networks, applications and computing infrastructure.
Cloud Engineer: Creates and manages cloud-based platforms and services.
Computer Networks Engineer: Works with network architecture, connectivity and infrastructure.
Data Engineer: Builds data pipelines, information-processing systems.
Systems Engineer: Integrates hardware and software and other technical elements.
Research and Development Engineer: Assists in the development and testing of new technology.

Common Questions Regarding Computer Engineering in Italy
Can Indian students pursue Masters in Computer Engineering in Italy?
Yes. Indian students with relevant bachelor's degrees can apply for admission to the university if they meet its academic, language and programme-specific admission requirements.
How Long Does a Master's in Computer Engineering Take in Italy?
Most Italian master's programs are two years long and have 120 ECTS. 2. Check the duration of the specific program on the university's official website.
Is it possible to Study Computer Engineering in Italy in English?

Yeah. Politecnico di Milano offers English-taught options such as the MSc in Computer Science and Engineering. The Politecnico di Torino and the University of Bologna also offer relevant programs, with a range of language options depending on the course.
How much does it cost to study Computer Engineering in Italy?

Tuition depends on the university and the students' situation. For example, the annual budgeting estimates are €1,000 (₹1,08,600), €2,500 (₹2,71,500), €5,000 (₹5,43,000), €8,000 (₹8,68,800). These are not official university fee quotations.
What can I do after a Master in Computer Engineering in Italy?

After the completion of the course, graduates can apply for the below job roles - Software Engineer Computer Engineer AI Engineer Embedded Systems Engineer Cybersecurity Engineer Cloud Engineer Data Engineer Career opportunities may depend on technical skills, experience, language proficiency and employer requirements.

faq.question: Is Computer Engineering taught in English in Italy?
faq.answer: Yes. Universities like Politecnico di Milano, Politecnico di Torino, and University of Padua offer English-taught Master of Science degrees in Computer Engineering.

faq.question: What is the duration of a Master's in Computer Engineering in Italy?
faq.answer: The programme requires 2 years of full-time academic study totaling 120 ECTS credits.

faq.question: What are the tuition fees for Computer Engineering in Italy?
faq.answer: Annual tuition at public universities is between €1,000 and €3,800, with income-based fee reductions and full DSU scholarships available.

faq.question: What is the difference between Computer Science and Computer Engineering in Italy?
faq.answer: Computer Engineering integrates computer hardware, digital electronic design, and embedded systems alongside advanced software engineering, whereas Computer Science emphasizes algorithms and software systems.

faq.question: What are the admission requirements for Indian students?
faq.answer: A Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related technical disciplines, strong academic marks, and English certification (IELTS 6.5+).

faq.question: What career paths are available after graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates work as embedded systems engineers, AI hardware designers, robotics specialists, network architects, and cybersecurity analysts across Europe.
